integrity: The graph decomposition is proved directly from ideal intersections via exponentwise maxima. True-twin classes give the sharp forcing lower bound and classify every minimum set. A two-dimensional Gram representation proves the rank witness. Polynomial equality reduces to a quadratic identity in the exponent sum, and the remaining Diophantine branch is classified completely.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to integer residue rings with exactly two distinct prime divisors.
The zero forcing polynomial depends only on the two exponents, not on the prime values.
The minimum-rank statement is over real symmetric graph-pattern matrices.
The values of zero forcing number and minimum rank have broader principal-ideal-ring coverage; the strengthened content is the full polynomial, minimizer classification, and exact collision theorem.
No assertion is made for three or more distinct prime factors.
title: Zero forcing polynomials of two-prime ideal-intersection graphs
